annotations.text:
SIGNAL — chosen 25 Aug 2026

One hero card carries the only number that matters; every album row below is a
detail of it. Mode is a coloured pill, and Archive is the one mode that gets a
warm colour, because it is the one that takes files off the phone.

Bottom pill nav replaces the four top tabs. Real album names, counts and sizes
throughout — taken off the Fold 4, not invented.

The hero inverts in dark rather than just darkening: on near-black the green
becomes the bright element, so it keeps its job of being the first thing the eye
lands on. Every other surface goes to a tinted near-black, and the status colours
lift in lightness so they stay legible instead of going muddy.

Dark is not a variant to add later here — it is the theme that shipped the
Teleprompter bug, so it gets designed alongside, not after.

STILL TO DRAW

• The deletion policy moving to Settings, with the review card on Albums.
• The foldable two-column layout — the device this mostly runs on.
• Restore, Syncing and Settings in dark.
• The empty state: a fresh install with nothing backed up, where the hero card has
  no number to be proud of and still has to look deliberate.
• Error and stopped states: drive full, signed out, network lost mid-run.

NOT CHOSEN — kept for reference

Quiet: editorial, hairline rules, no cards. Ages well, but status is easy to miss.
Console: dark and dense, monospaced. Most information per screen, narrow appeal,
  punishing at large font scales.
Tactile: soft lilac, big radii. The friendliest, and the only one that leads with
  reassurance rather than a number — but the softness can read as unserious for
  something moving 148 GB of someone's only copies.

One idea worth stealing from Tactile: leading with "nearly everything is safe"
rather than a raw count. Signal could carry that line above its number.

THE THREE DIALOGS — real copy, straight from strings.xml, not rewritten

Each gets a tinted icon tile rather than an alert triangle, and each pulls its single
most important sentence out of the paragraph into a tinted panel — that sentence is the
one people skip, and it is the one that makes the action legitimate.

Archive: warm, not red. This is a consent, not an error. The panel carries the standing-
instruction line — that files added later are covered too — because that is the part of
the mode people do not expect.

  Trimmed 25 Aug 2026 (Ian): the closing sentence — "the verified cloud copy is your
  guarantee, a local removal cannot be promised as recoverable" — moves to a Help /
  How-to screen. CLAUDE.md permits this: the cloud copy is what the UI MAY promise, not
  what it must say here, and a dialog short enough to be read beats one long enough to
  be skipped. But the second half of that sentence is a caution, not a promise, and it
  now sits somewhere the user need not visit before consenting. Help is therefore a
  surface that has to exist, not an optional extra — it is where a rule-bearing
  sentence went to live.

Deletion: red, and the panel is GREEN. The recycle bin sentence is the only promise the
app is allowed to make about a removal, so it gets the same colour as "protected".

Destination: a typed path, not a folder browser — browsing OneDrive is the thumbnail
browser the design principle rules out.

NOT OURS, AND MUST NOT BE COPIED: Android's own trash dialog on a local removal. It is
the platform's, capped at 2000 URIs per batch, and CLAUDE.md says it is not where the
consent comes from and must not be mirrored by an app-level prompt.

HELP IS THE FIRST-RUN GUIDE, RE-READABLE

Ian, 25 Aug 2026: the first-run guide frames Help too. Same topics, same order, so
someone who skipped setup finds exactly what they skipped rather than a differently
shaped FAQ that leaves them wondering what they missed.

One topic list serves three surfaces — the setup bubbles, this screen, and the
just-in-time prompt at first use. A topic is written once. TASK-014 already required
shared strings between the bubbles, Help and the Archive dialog, because three
descriptions of one irreversible operation drift apart invisibly.

Topics, not settings. Archive is its own entry rather than a bullet under modes: it is
the one that removes files, and the one the acknowledgement record gates.

Entry 5 is drawn expanded because it is the topic that made this screen necessary — it
holds the sentence the Archive dialog shed, and it is two panels: the promise, and
plainly the limit of the promise.

SETTINGS AND DEFAULTS — Ian, 25 Aug 2026

Sits apart from the numbered topics because it answers a different question. They explain
how the app works; this says what yours is set to right now.

It shows CURRENT values, not the factory list, and marks anything the user changed — the
destination row here is drawn as changed. A static list of defaults would not answer the
question someone actually opens this with, which is "what is my app doing?"

The green panel at the top is the headline from .claude/DEFAULTS.md: left alone, none of
these can remove a file from anywhere. It is the most reassuring sentence available and it
is true — two independent gates start closed, and Archive can never be a default.

The grace period is drawn greyed and labelled "not in use", because under the default
policy it governs nothing. Showing a live-looking setting with zero effect is its own
confusion — noted as open in DEFAULTS.md.

Source of truth for this screen is .claude/DEFAULTS.md. If a default changes, both move.

EACH ROW MUST ALSO SAY WHAT CHANGING IT DOES — Ian, same day. Not yet drawn:
rows expand to a second line covering the change, not just the current state.

One of them is retroactive and that is the surprise. Switching "when you delete a photo"
from Keep to Ask does not start watching from that moment — the missing-since timestamps
are recorded on every scan regardless of the policy, so flipping the switch REVEALS every
file already gone longer than the waiting period. Months of deletions in one list, on the
screen straight after a toggle.

So that row cannot just say "Ask". Before it is flipped it has to say how many files it
is about to surface — and the review list behind it has to stay sane at that size.

FOLD — Ian, 25 Aug 2026: keep the half-screen format and wrap the list into the other half,
rather than stretching rows across the width. Columns scroll together.

NOT list-detail. The standard large-screen pattern is two panes showing different things,
and it is the wrong one here: this app is two long lists, and what it wants from the width
is more rows, not a second pane.

The split is by COUNT, not row-major. Left holds the first half of the list, right the
second, and one scroll moves both. Each column therefore stays alphabetical top to bottom,
so you scan one and ignore the other. A row-major grid would put consecutive albums side by
side and make the eye zigzag for every item — worse for finding a name, which is the only
thing anyone does on this screen.

Two places the width is used differently rather than doubled:
• The top band. A hero card stretched to 880 looks sparse, so it takes half and the
  ready-to-remove callout takes the other. Both already exist on the phone.
• The nav bar is centred at phone width, not stretched. Four destinations spread across
  840px are a thumb-reach problem.

Applies to Album Modes and Restore only — they are the long lists. Settings, Syncing and
the dialogs cap their width and centre, or body text runs to 800px lines.

Album names are the real ones from the Fold 4; the two columns are not the true 1st and
46th entries, they are real rows placed to show the split.
